Next Steps @ NLL
At New Line Learning Academy, we passionately believe not only in preparing students academically for their public examinations, but also in helping them develop the skills required for their futures as citizens of the world. It is important that all students are fully supported and guided through the process of planning for their futures, and our PSHE, extra- and co-curricular provision reflects this. Careers support starts in the classroom, with all subject teachers playing an active role advising on career opportunities in their own subjects, and with form tutors delivering careers-related activities through the PSHE programme in personal development time. All students have the opportunity to complete a week’s work experience and to meet an independent careers advisor by the end of Year 11. In addition, students in all years have the opportunity to attend special events and enrichment activities, such as careers-themed assemblies, educational visits and trips to places of employment, the Higher Education evening and the school’s careers fair. The success of this CEIAG programme can be seen in the varied destinations of our student leavers.
For further information on our careers programme:
Contact our Careers Leader: Mr. Kemp
Email: akemp@newlinelearning.com

KS3
At Key stage 3 pupils will access careers fairs and PSHEE will incorporate careers information.
Further support is provided to Year 9 pupils, who will choose their GCSE options in this year. Support is provided through meetings with the academy leadership team building up the options evening and through some one-to-one support from Mr Kemp.
Pupils also access a careers fair where local, aspirational employers will present to all key stage 3 about the range of jobs available after education.
In line with the Gatsby Benchmarks, which set out best practice for schools, we are looking to develop more workplace encounters for pupils across KS3, particularly in STEM subjects
In year 9 some pupils will be selected to work with Think Forward to encourage them to develop the skills required for the workplace and to reduce pupils that end up ‘Not in education or Training’. (NEET)
Year 10
Support will be provided for Year 10 pupils choosing their next steps, through an initial Assembly in the Summer Term and then small group interviews held in school with Mr Kemp; these sessions will continue into Year 11.
Pupils will also have the opportunity to complete a work experience placement during the summer term, which is arranged by Mr Kemp.
Also, curriculum areas will be seeking to develop links between pupils’ studies and the world of work as we continue to develop our provision. Pupils can also make use of the careers resources in the Careers area.
Selected pupils will attend external careers fairs. Those pupils will selected to work with Think Forward to encourage them to develop the skills required for the workplace and to reduce pupils that end up ‘Not in education or Training’. (NEET) will continue to work with Coach Mark on a group and one-to-one basis.
Year 11
Each Year 11 pupil will be seen by Mr Kemp in a group interview for “Careers Guidance” before Christmas, following this, those pupils who need a little more help will be seen for a one to one interview. Part of the meeting will include information on when they need to make applications through the Area Prospectus : www.kentchoices4u.com.
Those pupils will selected to work with Think Forward to encourage them to develop the skills required for the workplace and to reduce pupils that end up ‘Not in education or Training’. (NEET) will continue to work with Coach Mark on a group and one-to-one basis.
If you feel your son or daughter will need a one to one interview, please let their form tutor or Mr Kemp know as soon as possible.
Pupils can also make use of the careers resources in the careers area.
Click on the logo to take you to the Unifrog login page.

pageCache.text:
Employers Careers Information
The importance of employer engagement with our pupils cannot be overstated.
Our pupils have numerous opportunities to engage with employers through events such as our whole school careers fair, and the Apprenticeship Event. Last year’s bi-annual careers fair featured over 30 stands, and students were guided on how to maximize this opportunity through a series of tutorials. The feedback from these events has been overwhelmingly positive.
We leverage the expertise of employers from diverse sectors—private, public, and voluntary—providing our students with a myriad of benefits. They gain insights into workplace dynamics, employer expectations, the importance of developing transferable skills, and the wide range of opportunities available to them. This engagement boosts their confidence and self-belief, educates them on what employers offer (apprenticeships, internships, scholarship programs, etc.), and helps them understand the steps needed to pursue their chosen careers.
We are continually seeking to expand our network of employer partnerships. To get involved, please contact Mr. Kemp: akemp@newlinelearning.com

pageCache.text:
Measuring and Assessing the Impact of the Careers Programme at New Line Learning
The careers programme in New Line Learning Academy is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of potential career paths, equip them with essential skills for the future workforce, and ensure they are well-informed when making decisions about their post-secondary education or employment options. The impact of the careers programme will be measured and assessed through both qualitative and quantitative methods, ensuring that the programme effectively supports student development and enhances career readiness.
Through these assessment methods, the careers programme will be continuously refined and improved to ensure that it meets the needs of all students and provides them with the tools and knowledge necessary to succeed in their future careers.

Personal Development Pathways
At New Line Learning, personal development is at the heart of everything we do. Every week throughout the academic year, students take part in our exciting Personal Development Pathways programme, designed to help them discover new interests, develop lifelong skills, and build confidence both inside and outside the classroom.
Our pathways provide students with unique opportunities to challenge themselves, work collaboratively, explore their passions, and develop the key skills needed for future success. Whether through physical activity, creativity, leadership, wellbeing, or community engagement, every pathway is carefully designed to support the development of well-rounded, resilient, and ambitious young people.
Our PHYSICAL Pathways
Students can develop teamwork, leadership, resilience, fitness, and independence through a range of active and practical experiences including Forest School, Food and Cookery, Elite Sport, and the Football Academy.
From learning outdoor survival and teamwork skills in Forest School to developing healthy lifestyles and practical life skills through cookery, students are encouraged to challenge themselves and grow in confidence. Elite Sport and Football Academy pathways allow students to further develop discipline, commitment, communication, and sporting excellence while representing the school with pride.
These experiences promote positive wellbeing, perseverance, and self-belief while encouraging students to remain active, engaged, and motivated.
Our Mental Pathways encourage creativity, focus, wellbeing, and personal expression through activities such as Creative Writing, Mindfulness, Craft Club, Games Club, Personal Finance, and Art.
Students are given opportunities to develop imagination, problem-solving, emotional wellbeing, and independence while exploring new hobbies and interests. Mindfulness sessions help students manage stress and build resilience, while Personal Finance supports the development of important life skills that will benefit students in the future.
Creative pathways also allow students to express themselves confidently, think critically, and develop a positive sense of identity through artistic and imaginative experiences.
Our Social Pathways help students strengthen communication, leadership, teamwork, empathy, and community awareness through experiences including Debate Club, School Hub, Tiger Reading, Nursery Support, Nurture, Language Ambassadors, Ancient History, and Community Support.
Students are encouraged to collaborate with others, share ideas confidently, support younger students, and contribute positively to the wider school community. These opportunities help students build meaningful relationships, develop leadership qualities, and grow into respectful and responsible young people.
Through participation in social pathways, students gain confidence in speaking, listening, mentoring, and teamwork while learning the importance of kindness, inclusion, and community engagement.
Our Year-Long Pathways
Students can also take part in exciting year-long pathways including School of Excellence, Gillingham Football Academy, Eco School, and Duke of Edinburgh.
These programmes provide students with exceptional opportunities to develop long-term commitment, resilience, leadership, and ambition. Whether working towards Duke of Edinburgh awards, promoting sustainability through Eco School, or developing elite sporting potential, students are encouraged to set goals, challenge themselves, and achieve their full potential.
The year-long pathways help students build independence, responsibility, confidence, and aspiration while creating memorable experiences that prepare them for future success both academically and personally.
Our Personal Development Pathways are a hugely important part of our school culture. They allow students to explore opportunities beyond the classroom, develop valuable life skills, broaden their experiences, and discover talents and interests that inspire them for the future. Above all, the programme helps every student to believe in themselves, achieve their goals, and become confident, well-rounded members of the school community.
For more information regarding our Pathway curriculum, please email: Mr Cooper pcooper@newlinelearning.com

Public Sector Equality Duty
Since the Equality Act became law in 2010, public bodies have been required by law to uphold a duty to promote disability, race and gender equality. In April 2011 this was replaced by a single public sector equality duty (known as the PSED or the equality duty). This new duty extends to all the aspects of a person’s identity – known as ‘protected characteristics’ – that are protected under the Equality Act 2010: race, disability, sex, age, religion or belief, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity and gender reassignment.
From April 2012 schools have been required to publish information annually, showing how they comply with this equality duty. Schools are also required to publish objectives linked to this duty at least once every four years. In complying with this duty, we are therefore committed to promoting strategies, opportunities, policies and procedures that will help us:
New Line Learning Equality Objectives
Eliminate discrimination, harassment, victimisation;
Remove or minimise disadvantages;
Take steps to meet different needs;
Encourage participation when it is disproportionately low;
